_description: App configuration plus schema documentation. The executable version of the schema is scripts/validate.py; if this file and the validator disagree, the validator wins and this file should be corrected.

courts._description: Every court code used anywhere (authority.court, applicable_courts, case session). 'kind' drives citation ordering (scotus, then circuit, then state) and which forum a court belongs to.

case_session_schema._description: Asked once at the start of the wizard, before any issue questions. Options use the same { id, label } shape as the question bank.

forum.prompt: Is this motion being filed in state or federal court?

state.note: Option ids are court codes from 'courts'. Only Alaska is in scope for now; adding a state means adding it to 'courts' and here.

federal_circuit.note: Option ids are court codes from 'courts'. Only the Ninth Circuit is in scope for now.

case_session_schema.answers: object keyed by question id; values are option ids (see question_types). A question the tree skipped is simply absent.

desired_courts: State court -> [SCOTUS, <state>]. Federal court -> [SCOTUS, <federal_circuit>]. SCOTUS binds both, so it is always included; circuit authority is never used in a state-court filing, and state authority is never used in a federal one.
_issues_note: Only id and file live here. Label, category, and everything else live in the issue file itself, so there is one place to edit. Output order is category_order first, then the order of this list within a category.

issue_schema.id: matches the file name and the manifest entry
issue_schema.label: internal/memo name for the issue, may include case names, e.g. '(Copelin/Zsupnik)'
issue_schema.motion_heading: court-facing argument heading for this section of the motion. Written as advocacy, no citations.
issue_schema.practice_notes: attorney-facing tips; rendered in the attorney memo, never in the motion
issue_schema.underscore_fields: Any key starting with '_' (e.g. '_author_notes') is a note to the author. Never rendered anywhere. The validator ignores underscore keys when checking for unknown fields.

values.unreviewed: Default for every new or edited issue. last_reviewed and reviewed_by must be empty.
values.reviewed: A lawyer has read the issue file and confirmed its rule statements and authorities are accurate and complete for every in-scope court the issue applies to. last_reviewed and reviewed_by must be filled in.

review_status.reset_on_edit: Any change to law_paragraph, trigger, or practice_notes should set status back to 'unreviewed'. Not yet enforced by tooling — git history is the audit trail for now.
review_status.why_no_circuits_reviewed: circuits_reviewed was removed. It tracked research for circuits but not states (AK had the same 'checked vs. not looked' ambiguity with no field), it generated a warning about the app's own research status, and with one circuit and one state in scope a single issue-level signoff covers the same ground. If multiple circuits or states come into scope later, per-court review status is the natural replacement.

applicable_courts_field.meaning: Which courts this issue is known to exist in at all, independent of how much content has been written.
applicable_courts_field.scotus_alone_is_universal: ['SCOTUS'] means the issue applies in every forum, because desired_courts always includes SCOTUS. Don't also list the circuit or state.
applicable_courts_field.state_or_circuit_only: List a specific court alone (e.g. ['AK']) when the issue rests on that court's own law and hasn't been confirmed anywhere else. Never generalize to 'any state'.
applicable_courts_field.effect: If desired_courts doesn't intersect applicable_courts, the issue is skipped entirely: its questions are never asked and nothing about it is rendered.

question_types.option_shape: multiple_choice and multi_select options are { id, label }. The id is stored in answers and referenced by conditions; the label is display text only and can be reworded freely.
question_types.id_stability_rule: Never change an id once conditions reference it — change only the label. If an option's meaning changes, give it a new id and update every condition that used the old one.
question_types.yes_no: No options array. Answer is 'yes' or 'no'.
question_types.multi_select: Answer is an array of option ids (possibly empty).
question_types.short_text: Free text. Never referenced in a condition.

condition_shape.description: Used by match_condition, review_conditions[].when, excluded_explanations[].when, and rule_statements[].when. Either a leaf { question, op, value } or a compound { all: [...] } / { any: [...] }; compounds can nest. Values are option ids, never labels.
condition_shape.unanswered_questions: If a leaf's question is absent from answers (skipped by the tree or left blank), the leaf evaluates to false — for every op, including not_equals, not_in, not_includes, and empty. A condition can only be satisfied by answers the attorney actually gave.

ops_for_scalar_answers.in: answer is in value (list of ids)
ops_for_scalar_answers.not_in: answer is not in value (list of ids)

ops_for_array_answers.includes: value (single id) is in the answer array
ops_for_array_answers.not_includes: value (single id) is not in the answer array
ops_for_array_answers.not_empty: at least one option selected; no value

rule_statements_schema.description: law_paragraph.rule_statements is an ordered list. Each statement is one proposition (a sentence, two at most) with its own authorities. The rendered paragraph is the statements that survive filtering, in order.

shape.text: the bare proposition. Never embed a case name or citation, even mid-sentence. May be a direct quotation.
shape.when: optional condition. If present, the statement renders only when it evaluates true. Use it for facts that change which propositions belong in the motion — e.g. which remedy applies, or a point that only matters if a relative (not an attorney) was requested.
shape.authorities: see authority_schema; every authority supports exactly this statement's text

rule_statements_schema.filtering: A statement renders only if (1) its when is absent or true, and (2) at least one of its authorities is for a desired court. If (1) holds but (2) fails, the statement is dropped from the motion and listed in the memo as a gap, so the attorney knows a relevant proposition is missing.
rule_statements_schema.use_when_for_advocacy: A defense motion shouldn't volunteer propositions that help the prosecution unless the facts make them unavoidable. Example: in denial-of-contact-before-breath-test, the 'reasonable time' balancing statement renders only when timing is actually disputed, not when the request was denied outright.

shape.name: case name, or the statute/rule/constitutional provision identifier
shape.citation: cases: '<volume> <reporter> <first page> (<court> <year>)', e.g. '435 P.3d 975 (Alaska App. 2018)'. Non-cases: empty string, since the name is the citation.
shape.pincite: cases only, required key: the pinpoint page(s) for THIS statement's proposition, e.g. '354' or '90-91'. Empty string until researched. Because authorities live on individual statements, the same case can carry different pincites in different statements.
shape.court: a code from 'courts' — whose law this is, not literally which court decided it (AK statutes are 'AK')

authority_schema.rendering: Case: '*Name*, <volume reporter first-page>, <pincite> (<court year>)' — the pincite is inserted before the parenthetical, and omitted if empty. Non-case: 'Name'. Multiple authorities on one statement are joined with '; ', ordered SCOTUS, then circuit, then state — this produces parallel citations such as '*Rodriguez v. United States*, 575 U.S. 348 (2015); *Simmons v. State*, 435 P.3d 975 (Alaska App. 2018)'.
authority_schema.not_yet_supported: Short forms (Id., short case names on repeat citations) and signals (See, see also, cf.). A paragraph that cites the same case in several statements repeats the full citation each time.

motion.audience: The court. Copy-ready text for the argument section of the attorney's own motion template.
motion.contents: An 'ARGUMENT' heading, then one numbered section per included issue (I, II, III...) with the issue's motion_heading and its rendered law paragraph. Nothing else: no notes, no brackets, no practice tips, no internal labels.
motion.empty_case: If no issue matched, the motion contains only a line saying so, and the memo explains.

sections: Case settings: forum and which courts' authority was used.

Included issues, numbered to match the motion: the issue label, any review_conditions notes that fired, practice notes, gaps (statements dropped for lack of authority in this forum), a coverage note when a SCOTUS-grounded section cites no circuit/state authority, and a flag if the issue's content is unreviewed.
Issues considered but not included: excluded_explanations that fired, under each issue's label.
Reminders for every motion: cross_cutting_reminders, whenever at least one issue was included.

rendering_logic: 2. Walk issues in output order (category_order, then manifest list order).
3. Skip any issue whose applicable_courts doesn't intersect courts.

4. If match_condition is true: render the law paragraph (see rule_statements_schema filtering). Collect review_conditions whose when is true, practice_notes, gaps, and the coverage/unreviewed flags for the memo. If every statement was filtered out, the issue goes in the memo as 'matched, but no law paragraph is available in this forum' and is left out of the motion.
5. If match_condition is false: collect excluded_explanations whose when is true, for the memo. Check these for every unmatched issue, every time.
6. Number the issues that produced a paragraph, render motion and memo.

cross_cutting_reminders.display_note: Before relying on any issue in the motion, confirm the defendant has standing to challenge it — a reasonable expectation of privacy in the place or thing searched. Standing is assessed separately for each issue; having it for one doesn't establish it for another.

For each issue, consider whether the evidence you're seeking to suppress is a direct or derivative product of that violation, or sufficiently attenuated to survive suppression even if the violation is found.

field_audience_convention.motion_text: motion_heading and rule statement text/authorities. Written for the court.
field_audience_convention.memo_text: practice_notes, review_conditions[].display_note, excluded_explanations[].display_note, cross_cutting_reminders. Written for the attorney.
field_audience_convention.author_notes: Anything starting with '_'. Written for whoever maintains the content — what's unverified, what still needs research, why something is structured a certain way. Never rendered.
field_audience_convention.test: Would an attorney want this sentence in front of the court? Motion. In front of themselves while deciding what to file? Memo. Is it really about the state of the file? Author note.
field_audience_convention.flag_vs_display_note: 'flag' is a short machine id for logging; never render it.

validation: Run `python3 scripts/validate.py` from the repo root before every commit. Errors mean something is broken; warnings are worth reading but may be intentional. `python3 -m unittest discover tests` checks that the validator still catches every known class of bug.
